buttonLabel: "Explore adventures in Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador"
lead: >-
  At Iguazu, you follow walking paths alongside the waterfalls; in Chile, you prepare for the high-altitude leg; and in the Galápagos, you head out to sea and explore the islands. The main 4x4 journey through lagoons and Uyuni takes place in Bolivia, outside the four countries in this filter. Compare the activities, transfers and physical demands.
---
## What makes this adventure itinerary special

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It visits Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador, as well as Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia. **Selecting four countries does not mean this is a separate four-country itinerary**.

The defining feature of the journey is the changing nature of the activities. At Iguazu, there are walks through national parks; in the Andes, high-altitude journeys in off-road vehicles; and in the Galápagos, boat trips and nature trails. The four named countries do not include a mandatory volcano ascent, technical trekking expedition or white-water rafting. Compare other formats in the [multi-country adventure catalog](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

## Brazil and Argentina: walking trails and an optional boat trip

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the itinerary includes Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and sightseeing excursions. After flying to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), you explore the waterfalls on foot. The following day brings the [Argentine side of Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), where trails and viewing platforms take you closer to the falling water.

A more active extra is the [Macuco Safari](/brazil/foz-do-iguacu/macuco-safari-program-forest-boat/), which combines a forest segment with a motorboat ride. It **costs extra** and is not among the mandatory waterfall excursions. The word “safari” should not be interpreted as a guarantee of wildlife sightings.

The Argentine days after Iguazu focus on Buenos Aires, tango and urban history. They provide a change of pace after the nature visits, without a separate challenging hike on the itinerary.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama before the highlands

From [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), you fly to Calama and travel to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) to acclimatize. An evening astronomy excursion with telescopes is offered as an optional activity, but it has an additional charge and depends on operating conditions.

The most expedition-like portion begins the next day **in Bolivia**: two days in 4x4 vehicles through lagoons, geysers and the Uyuni Salt Flat. The route reaches elevations above 4,000 m and includes expedition-style accommodation. These activities should not be counted as Chilean experiences simply because the journey starts in Atacama.

Gradual adaptation, appropriate pacing and how you feel are all important at altitude. Even excellent physical fitness does not guarantee protection against altitude sickness. If this section raises concerns, discuss its route and elevations rather than arbitrarily shortening a city excursion.

## Ecuador: the Galápagos by boat and on island trails

The Ecuadorian segment begins in Quito and at the equator, followed by a flight to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), the itinerary includes uplands inhabited by giant tortoises and lava tunnels.

The day at sea follows **one of two alternative routes**: [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas, or [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrión. The descriptions include walks, swimming and possible snorkeling. Scuba diving is not scheduled here and should not be promised.

Boarding the boat, weather conditions and individual susceptibility to seasickness may affect this day more than physical fitness. Stable footwear is useful for the walks, along with sun protection and respect for the islands' wildlife.

## Coordinating physical demands and flights

The itinerary brings together humid Iguazu, dry Atacama, high-altitude Bolivia and oceanic islands. It involves numerous flights and border crossings. When choosing the trip, assess not only its total duration but also travel time, acclimatization, rest after active days and the possibility of rescheduling a sea excursion in unfavorable conditions.

This journey suits travelers seeking **a comprehensive sightseeing expedition with occasional active experiences**. If you want a series of sporting hikes, compare [specialist adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/) and [all tours through this four-country combination](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile_ecuador/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need mountaineering experience?

The itinerary features walks and drives, not a mandatory technical ascent. Bolivia's high-altitude segment still requires careful acclimatization.

### Is Macuco Safari included in the tour price?

No. It is an optional paid activity near Iguazu Falls on the Brazilian side.

### Can I visit both Seymour and South Plaza?

Only one alternative sea excursion is included. The tour does not promise to cover both routes.

lead: >-
  Rio de Janeiro, Buenos Aires, Santiago and Quito reveal different chapters of South American history: Brazil's Portuguese heritage, immigrant neighborhoods and tango, Chilean city squares, and Ecuadorian colonial Baroque. The extended itinerary includes specific excursions in these cities, followed by nature-focused stages.

## The cultures of four countries on one extended itinerary

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). In addition to Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador, the itinerary includes Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia. That means further cultural stops as well as travel days. **The four countries selected in the filter are not the tour's complete itinerary**.

This journey shows how individual city tours differ. Rio features colonial buildings and the city's famous landmarks; Buenos Aires, historic neighborhoods and tango; Santiago, its political center and public squares; and Quito, architecture shaped by both European and local traditions. The [general collection for these four countries](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile_ecuador/) also covers other themes.

## Brazil: Rio between the bay and the old city

After São Paulo, the journey continues to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The itinerary includes Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain, and a sightseeing tour through central neighborhoods, churches and historic buildings. These excursions reveal both the city's iconic sights and the heritage of old Rio.

This tour does not confirm a separate day in a history museum, a meeting with Carnival participants, or a cooking workshop. If a particular museum or cultural encounter is your main goal, allow additional time for it. The journey then heads to [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where nature becomes the focus.

## Argentina: Buenos Aires neighborhoods and an evening of tango

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a sightseeing tour takes in La Boca, [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/), Plaza de Mayo, Recoleta and modern neighborhoods. Squares, markets and former port districts reveal different sides of the Argentine capital's past.

A [tango show with dinner](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-dinner-transfer/) is scheduled for the evening. This is an actual included event, not just a general suggestion to go to the theater. It complements daytime sightseeing with a living city tradition.

The following day includes a ferry to Montevideo. That is Uruguay, a separate country with its own sightseeing day in the full itinerary.

## Chile: Santiago from La Moneda to Santa Lucía

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the tour introduces the La Moneda government building, Plaza de Armas, the cathedral and Santa Lucía Hill, followed by modern neighborhoods. This offers a concrete contrast with Buenos Aires: the Argentine day emphasizes neighborhoods and tango; the Chilean day emphasizes the historic center and civic architecture.

The next stop, [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), prepares travelers for the highlands. No specialized archaeological excursion within Chile is promised for that day. The full route later visits Tiwanaku in Bolivia and Inca monuments in Peru, but **those sites are not in Chile**.

## Ecuador: Quito's Baroque architecture before the Galápagos

Ecuador includes a sightseeing day in Quito and at the equator. You explore the historic center, the Basilica of the National Vow, churches and squares, then Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan Museum. Quito's historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; its Baroque tradition combines European and local artistic influences.

Experiments presented in the tourist-oriented Intiñan Museum should be understood as museum demonstrations, not proof of the equator's precise physical location. For a meaningful introduction to history and geography, focus on architecture, collections and the content of the guided visit.

Next comes a flight to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), where wildlife and boat trips take center stage. This is a valuable contrast, but those nature days should not be portrayed as a continuation of the urban history itinerary.

## Who will enjoy this combination?

This extended itinerary suits travelers who want to see several capitals, pre-Columbian monuments in additional countries and iconic natural attractions. If history and museums are your main priority, consider spending more time in one or two cities and comparing [Culture and History journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/) with [themed tours in Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a tango show included?

Yes. Buenos Aires includes a daytime sightseeing tour and a separate evening tango show with dinner.

### Will travelers see Quito's historic center?

Yes. The sightseeing day includes the old city's churches and squares, followed by Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan Museum.

### Are Tiwanaku and Machu Picchu in the four selected countries?

No. Both appear on the longer tour, but they are located in Bolivia and Peru, respectively.

  The two sides of Iguazu Falls, a stop in Chile's Atacama Desert and nature excursions in the Galápagos are distinct stages of a much longer trip. It is important to distinguish nature-focused days from transit days and remember that only one of two alternative island boat excursions is scheduled.

## Nature in Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador: what the trip includes

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} covering the four named countries with a nature-focused itinerary. The [32-day, eight-country South American journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also includes Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia. The four countries in the filter **do not constitute a separate short trip limited to those destinations**.

Natural experiences are distributed unevenly across the days. In Argentina and Brazil, you visit Iguazu; in Chile, you stop in San Pedro de Atacama before the high-altitude Bolivian segment; and in Ecuador, you visit Santa Cruz and one of the island excursion routes. Between Chile and Ecuador, the actual itinerary includes Bolivia's lagoons, Uyuni, Titicaca and the Peruvian Andes. They cannot be removed from the itinerary just because they do not appear in this collection's title.

The logistics and cultural program are described in the [general Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador collection](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile_ecuador/). Here, we focus on the natural landscapes and conditions for visiting them.

## Iguazu: why both sides matter

After Rio, you fly to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). In the Brazilian sector, the itinerary includes a tour of the waterfalls with a Russian-speaking guide. This is followed by the [Argentine side near Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), after which you fly to Buenos Aires.

The Brazilian viewpoints reveal the overall width of the cascades and panoramic views of the forested banks. Walkways on the Argentine side lead closer to the flowing water from different directions. Both sectors belong to protected forest environments, but the main purpose is to experience the waterfalls. The itinerary does not promise a separate multi-day forest expedition.

Allow time for the international border crossing and take walking-trail conditions into account. Access to individual sections may vary according to weather and water levels. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are listed as **optional paid activities** and should not be treated as included simply because they are close to the waterfalls.

Another natural highlight in Brazil is [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/) on the route to Corcovado in Rio. Forested slopes and city panoramas feature on the sightseeing excursion, but specialist wildlife watching is not a separate mandatory service.

## Chilean Atacama: scenery and transit are not the same thing

From Santiago, you fly to Calama and travel to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This stop prepares you for the onward journey into high-altitude Bolivia. An evening astronomy excursion is possible, but optional and subject to separate confirmation.

Atacama is known for its arid climate and open volcanic landscapes. Yet stopping in San Pedro **does not mean that a day visiting Moon Valley, the Atacama Salt Flat or other desert attractions is included**. If Chile's natural scenery is your main objective, compare [nature tours in Chile](/interests/nature/tours/chile/) and arrange additional visits in a custom itinerary.

Beyond the Chilean border, a two-day off-road program begins in Bolivia, visiting high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni. Some sections exceed 4,000 m. Although Bolivia is not named in this filter, its inclusion substantially affects preparation, clothing and overnight stays for the whole trip.

## Ecuador: Santa Cruz and two alternatives for the day at sea

You fly from Peru to Quito and then to Baltra. The transfer across [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) leads to Puerto Ayora. In the [Santa Cruz Highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/), the scheduled activities include observing giant tortoises and exploring lava tunnels. This is the most clearly specified nature activity during the first part of the island visit.

The following day takes you to other parts of the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). **One of two excursions is selected**: North Seymour with Bachas Beach, or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. Both concern island wildlife, but the itinerary does not promise both routes on the same day. Encounters with seabirds, iguanas and sea lions in their natural habitat depend on the location, timing and animal behavior.

Visitors must follow protected-area rules: remain on permitted paths, keep their distance from wildlife, and never touch or feed animals. Biosecurity checks on luggage and food apply on arrival in the islands. Current documents, conservation fees and which costs are included should be checked before travel.

## Preparing for humidity, altitude and sea conditions

Iguazu is humid and full of spray; Atacama has drier air and pronounced day-to-night temperature changes; the Galápagos require attention to sun exposure, sea conditions and visitor rules. A generic suggestion to “pack for South America” is useless here: choose clothing according to the actual nature excursions.

A further feature of the **real eight-country route** is the altitude of Bolivia and Peru between Chile and Ecuador. Someone comfortable at the waterfalls or in Rio may respond very differently in the highlands. Seek medical advice in advance if you have relevant health limitations.

| Nature destination | What to check |
|---|---|
| Iguazu | Both sides, trail access and the border |
| Atacama | Whether a dedicated desert excursion is included |
| Galápagos | Which boat route is confirmed |
| Andes | Elevations and time for acclimatization |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Choosing the right nature itinerary

An extended tour lets you experience several kinds of landscape in a single vacation, but it also involves many city days, flights and additional countries. If you want longer in the Chilean desert or more island excursions, the duration and transport arrangements will have to change.

Compare [multi-country nature journeys](/multi-country/interests/nature/) and [nature tours in Ecuador](/interests/nature/tours/ecuador/). The decisive factor is not the number of countries in the heading, but the actual natural attractions and time allotted to them.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in four countries

### Are both sides of Iguazu included?

Yes. Separate sightseeing days cover the Brazilian and Argentine sides.

### Will there be a dedicated nature excursion in Atacama?

The stop in San Pedro is included, but separate trips to desert attractions have not been confirmed. An astronomy evening is offered as an optional extra.

### Can I take both Galápagos boat excursion routes?

No. The itinerary includes one of the two alternatives, to be agreed separately.

### Why do I have to prepare for Bolivia?

Because the full itinerary crosses its high-altitude regions between Chile and Peru, even if those countries do not appear in the filter.

At Iguazu you see rainforest and waterfalls, in Chile the Atacama Desert, while the main wildlife experience takes place in the Galápagos: giant tortoises on Santa Cruz and one of two alternative boat excursions to islands with seabirds, iguanas and sea lions.

## Where the wildlife experiences are concentrated in four countries

Our collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [32-day itinerary through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It visits Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador, along with Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia. Some nature encounters along the complete route, such as flamingos at high-altitude lagoons, take place in Bolivia. They should not be attributed to Chile just because the border is nearby.

For wildlife travel, the key question is **where dedicated animal watching is planned and where the itinerary simply visits an attractive park or viewpoint**. The [general collection for these four countries](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile_ecuador/) explains the geography; here we focus on nature observations.

## Iguazu: forest on the Brazilian and Argentine sides

In [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), excursions cover both sides of the waterfalls. The subtropical forests surrounding the cascades are rich in plants and wildlife, but the principal route uses park walkways and viewing platforms. Sightings of rare animals are not guaranteed.

On the Brazilian side, you can add the [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) and the [Macuco Safari](/brazil/foz-do-iguacu/macuco-safari-program-forest-boat/), which includes a boat trip toward the waterfalls. Both are **paid extras** under the approved itinerary. The Bird Park introduces birds in enclosures; it is not wildlife watching in the wild. Macuco Safari is primarily a forest excursion and motorboat ride to the falls, not a safari searching for animals.

After Iguazu, the itinerary continues through cities and cultural experiences, including Buenos Aires. Simply including those stops does not create further wildlife-watching activities.

## Chile: Atacama's landscapes and altitude preparation

After Santiago, you arrive in Calama and drive to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The itinerary uses this stop for acclimatization. There is no dedicated Chilean safari here. The next day, the expedition crosses Bolivia via high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni, where the descriptions mention flamingos. That is **another country**, with its own conditions for traveling at elevation.

The transition between ecosystems is interesting in itself, but wildlife-focused travelers should distinguish fauna observations from landscape sightseeing.

## Ecuador: Santa Cruz Highlands and giant tortoises

The principal wildlife experience begins in the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). After landing on Baltra, you cross to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The itinerary includes an excursion to the [Santa Cruz Highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) to see giant tortoises and lava tunnels. Travelers then stay in Puerto Ayora.

The Galápagos are famous for endemic species, seabirds, iguanas and sea lions. But observations take place in a protected natural environment: keep your distance, stay on authorized trails and follow the guides' instructions. Even on these islands, no particular animal or behavior can be guaranteed on a schedule.

## One day at sea, two different options

**Option: North Seymour and Bachas.** [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) is described as having colonies of frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies. The visit continues to Bachas Beach, with its lagoon and opportunities to swim or snorkel. You may observe sea lions, birds and iguanas, but sightings depend on nature.

**Option: South Plaza and Cape Carrión.** On [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/), the plan includes a walk near sea lions and land iguanas, and watching seabirds. The next stop is Cape Carrión, with possible snorkeling.

These are **alternative routes** for the same included day. The tour does not promise both; the specific excursion is confirmed after booking. Choose based on the wildlife you hope to observe, sea conditions and actual visitor access.

## When to choose the extended tour versus a Galápagos-focused trip

On the 32-day journey, several days are allocated to the Galápagos, with one day at sea following an alternative excursion route. The rest is devoted to Iguazu, cities, the Andes and other countries. This is a good option for combining nature with extensive geography.

For a longer wildlife-watching experience, compare [wildlife and safari tours in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) and [other multi-country wildlife itineraries](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/). If waterfalls and desert scenery are your priorities, explore [nature tours across these four countries](/multi-country/argentina_brazil_chile_ecuador/interests/nature/). More island days offer more opportunities, but specific wildlife sightings remain natural encounters, not guaranteed services.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Santa Cruz tortoises included?

Yes. An excursion into the Santa Cruz Highlands to see giant tortoises is part of the itinerary.

### Can we visit both island alternatives?

No. The itinerary includes North Seymour and Bachas **or** South Plaza and Cape Carrión.

### Is snorkeling available?

Both alternative descriptions mention the possibility of snorkeling. Check equipment and conditions for the confirmed excursion. Scuba diving is not listed.

## Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Peru: which itineraries are available?

Four South American countries bring together very different parts of the continent. [Brazil](/brazil/) opens the journey with coastal [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). [Argentina](/argentina/) continues with the other side of the falls and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). In [Chile](/chile/), travelers can explore [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and the Pacific coast, while [Peru](/peru/) rounds out the journey with [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the Sacred Valley and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/).

Our collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with all four countries as **principal destinations on the route**. One is the [15-day Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/), which does not require a visit to Bolivia. Other current itineraries also pass through Bolivia, so they take longer and include Chile's Atacama Desert, high-altitude lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat.

**The main decision:** choose exactly four countries on a more compact trip, or five countries with an additional high-altitude stage. Distances between nearby points may look short on a map, but the journey actually combines long flights, airport changes and overland crossings through the Andes.

## How the 15-day itinerary works without Bolivia

The [15-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) begins in Rio. Several days are devoted to the city, Corcovado, the Christ the Redeemer statue and Sugarloaf Mountain. A flight to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) follows. The waterfalls are explored from both the Brazilian and Argentine sides: these are two distinct parks and two separate visits involving an international border.

After [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), the journey continues to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and then [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The Chilean section includes an excursion to [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) on the Pacific coast. Next comes a flight to Peru, the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), a train journey to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and the conclusion in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

This version **does not include the Uyuni Salt Flat in Bolivia or a separate Atacama Desert leg as mandatory activities**. That distinction matters: listing the same four countries in a catalog title does not mean all the tours visit the same places in Chile and Peru.

The format requires successive transfers and flights. Under the current description, international tickets and domestic flights along the Rio – Iguazu – Buenos Aires – Santiago – Cusco – Lima chain are excluded from the basic 15-day offer. When comparing it with five-country itineraries, check which flight tickets are included rather than looking only at starting prices.

## When it makes sense to add a fifth country: Bolivia

On the [18-day five-country group journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), Brazil and Argentina are followed by [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The high-altitude Bolivian stage then begins, with colorful lagoons, off-road driving and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). After La Paz and Lake Titicaca, the journey continues through Peru to Cusco and Machu Picchu.

The Bolivian segment changes the trip substantially: it brings off-road travel, dust, temperature swings, nights at altitude and more time away from major cities. This is not a brief optional excursion that can be slipped into the compact 15-day itinerary without consequences. It is better to select a dedicated five-country program from the outset and account for its physical demands.

Five-country tours also differ in dates and format: there is a [private Carnival trip](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/), a [New Year group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) and a [Champions' Parade journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/). Carnival dates affect the start of the journey and accommodation availability in Rio. Before choosing, compare actual departure dates and events included: the word “Carnival” in another tour's name does not guarantee the same activities.

## Borders, flights and documentation

As of **October 15, 2026**, short tourist visits by Russian citizens with valid international passports to **Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru** are permitted without national visas under the respective bilateral arrangements. Official information for each of these four countries indicates an allowance of up to 90 days within a 180-day period. However, each country makes its own immigration decision and has its own passport and entry-document rules. Visa-free travel does not guarantee admission at the border.

This journey requires checking **at least two international border crossings around Iguazu**: the Brazilian and Argentine parks lie in different countries. For a Russian traveler, this generally does not change visa-free status, but it does affect passport control, excursion timing and the next flight.

If a ticket involves a connection in a country that is not part of the tour, the **transit requirements** must be checked separately for Russian nationality and the airport arrangement. The same word “connection” may mean an airside transfer or passing immigration again to collect luggage. We help assemble the flight sequence, review each traveler's documentation requirements and allow sensible gaps between independently booked tickets.

Five-country journeys add Bolivia and its own border procedures on the Atacama–highland lagoons leg. Visa information for only the four countries on this page cannot be applied to a journey that actually includes a fifth.

## Climate: why one suitcase must suit different seasons

The route spans Brazil's humid Atlantic coast, the temperate latitudes of Argentina and Chile, the Pacific coast and Peru's Andes. “Summer in South America” therefore says little about the weather at every stop.

| Stage | What to expect |
|---|---|
| Rio and Iguazu | Heat, humidity and downpours |
| Buenos Aires | Seasonal changes between heat and cool weather |
| Santiago and the coast | Drier summers and cool evenings |
| Cusco and Machu Picchu | Elevation, rain and changeable weather |

Around December and January, for example, Rio can be hot and humid while Santiago is in its summer season. That can coincide with more frequent rains in high-altitude Peru. Between May and September, the Cusco area tends to be drier, but southern cities in Argentina and Chile are cooler. Choose your dates around **the experience that matters most**, rather than looking for a universal ideal season that does not exist.

For the 15-day journey, pack light clothing for Rio, shoes with good grip for Iguazu and Machu Picchu, sun and rain protection, a windbreaker for the coast and a warm layer for Andean evenings. The five-country option with Atacama and Bolivia requires additional warm clothing suitable for cold high-altitude conditions. We help tailor a packing list to the actual route so that unnecessary winter clothes do not fill your luggage on the four-country trip.

Carry-on and checked baggage limits on domestic flights may differ from those on the long-haul ticket. This matters especially when segments are operated by different airlines or are not included in one booking.

## Cusco's altitude, health and visiting Machu Picchu

[Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is approximately 3,350 m above sea level. Even physically fit travelers may feel the effects of altitude after arriving quickly from lowlands. On the 15-day itinerary, the Chilean leg is followed by arrival in Cusco and an onward drive into the Sacred Valley. The valley lies below central Cusco, but an individual acclimatization plan should still be discussed in advance.

The risk of altitude sickness depends on sleeping elevation, rate of ascent and personal tolerance. Headache, nausea or unusual breathlessness should prompt timely assessment rather than automatic further ascent. Travelers with heart or lung conditions, pregnant travelers and people with physical limitations should seek medical advice specific to the planned elevations. The highlands of Bolivia require even more careful preparation on five-country itineraries.

A visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is subject to particular tickets and visitor routes. Peru's Ministry of Culture operates several official circuits: panoramic, classic and routes with separate ascents. **A ticket for one circuit does not grant access to every other area**. Agree on the date, time, ticket type and train to Aguas Calientes before booking; without confirmation, a freely chosen route inside the site cannot be promised.

Medical considerations in tropical parts of Brazil and Peru differ from high-altitude risks. Discuss yellow fever recommendations with your doctor according to the regions visited and previous countries, along with insect-bite prevention and insurance coverage. Requirements for proof of vaccination and recommendations for personal health are different matters and should be checked separately.

## Currencies, cards and the real four-country budget

Four local currencies appear along the route: **the Brazilian real, Argentine peso, Chilean peso and Peruvian sol**. The tour itself may be priced in US dollars, but everyday expenses in restaurants, cafes and pharmacies follow the payment practices of the country you are visiting. There is no universal exchange rate or guaranteed acceptance of US dollars at every stop.

Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks do not provide normal international payment services abroad. Travelers from Russia should check their foreign-issued cards, cash-withdrawal fees, account currencies and an independent financial backup in advance. Not every ATM dispenses the required banknotes, and payment conditions can vary even between neighboring countries. We help coordinate how to pay for the journey and explain where local cash may be needed, without guaranteeing that a particular bank's card will work.

**Comparing prices means comparing what is included.** The 15-day tour lists accommodation with breakfast, excursions, transfers and specified entrance tickets as part of the offer, but international and domestic flights are excluded from the basic price. On the [18-day five-country group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), domestic flights, by contrast, are explicitly included. Comparing two “from” prices alone can be misleading. Compare tickets, hotel nights, excursions, language of assistance and whether the tour is private or group-based.

## Who should choose this journey, and who might prefer a shorter route?

**Fifteen days and four countries** suit travelers who want to see major cultural and natural attractions on one trip, are comfortable taking several flights and do not plan a multi-day off-road expedition. For first-time visitors to South America, this itinerary alternates major cities and nature, but leaves relatively little free time.

**Eighteen to nineteen days and five countries** make more sense if Atacama, Uyuni and travel across the Andes are priorities. Stamina, altitude tolerance and readiness for long transfers matter more. Celebrating New Year or Carnival determines dates for the entire journey, not just one evening in Rio.

For families with young children, older travelers and people who find it difficult to change hotels every few days, we can discuss a slower pace and fewer stops. That is a custom arrangement, not a promise to change the contents of a published group tour without changing its terms.

## Answers to common questions about the trip

### Is there a ready-made itinerary covering exactly four countries, without Bolivia?

Yes. The [15-day Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) covers only these four principal countries. Other itineraries in the collection include Bolivia, with different logistics and physical demands.

### Can I add Uyuni to the 15-day program?

Adding the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) means a separate Bolivian segment with travel, overnight stays and altitude. It is better to compare the existing [five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) or discuss rebuilding a private itinerary than to assume Uyuni can be fitted in as a short excursion between Santiago and Cusco.

### Does a Russian citizen need four visas?

Visa-free agreements apply to ordinary short tourist visits to Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru, as checked on October 15, 2026. A valid passport and compliance with national entry rules are still required, while visa requirements for transit countries must be checked separately.

### Can I visit both sides of Iguazu in one day?

On some routes this is logistically possible, but both sides require time, appropriate entrance tickets and border procedures. On the [15-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/), the Brazilian and Argentine visits are arranged within the program before onward travel to Buenos Aires. The actual itinerary of the selected tour takes priority over a blanket promise to “see everything in one day.”

### When should I book Machu Picchu?

Before finalizing flights and overnight stays in Peru, confirm an available day and the specific official visitor circuit. Tickets are sold for particular times and areas, so leaving this decision until your arrival in Cusco is risky.

### What most often increases the budget?

Additional flights, differences between private and group travel, optional excursions and alterations to include Bolivia. Exclusions differ between tours, so the final quote must be based on actual services rather than multiplying a “from” price by the number of participants.
